detail.longDescription: I created a set of test files that looks like this. ./ ├── a │ ├── file1.txt │ └── file3.txt ├── b │ ├── file2.txt │ └── file4.txt Where the contents of file1 and file4 are exactly the same (via cp ). When I run a script in python to generate their hashes, I get different behavior depending on the location of the hashlib.md5() assignment. Working example: import hashlib import glob PATH = "/home/wes/Documents/foldertest/" # md5 = hashlib.md5() for eachfile in glob.glob(PATH + '*/*'): md5 = hashlib.md5() with open(eachfile, 'rb') as infile: data = infile.read() md5.update(data) print(md5.hexdigest()) produces the output: 5149d403009a139c7e085405ef762e1a 3d709e89c8ce201e3c928eb917989aef 60b91f1875424d3b4322b0fdd0529d5d 5149d403009a139c7e085405ef762e1a But this script: import hashlib import glob PATH = "/home/wes/Documents/foldertest/" md5 = hashlib.md5() for eachfile in glob.glob(PATH + '*/*'): # md5 = hashlib.md5() with open(eachfile, 'rb') as infile: data = infile.read() md5.update(data) print(md5.hexdigest()) produces incorrect output: 5149d403009a139c7e085405ef762e1a 0c5a1e3bcd9f8636a73d424b1e68dd3b febdf731804fc46d60a4378888a32451 18a68ddeeb0ea523c8560108b99e1774 What happens to the hash of file4 when I change move the location of the assignment?
